name: Pellucid Marginal Degeneration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Topographic Diagnostic Criteria for Pellucid Marginal Degeneration

criteria.description: Presence of a characteristic inferior peripheral band of corneal thinning 1-2 mm from the limbus
Corneal topography showing characteristic 'kissing dove' or 'crab claw' pattern with inferior steepening
Absence of corneal scarring or vascularization differentiating from other ectatic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of inferior peripheral corneal thinning with characteristic corneal topography patterns
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by corneal topography; differentiation from keratoconus is essential.

searchTerms: thinning of lower edge of cornea

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic 'kissing dove' or 'crab claw' pattern on corneal topography
searchTerms: cornea shape like 'kissing dove' or 'crab claw'

common.symptomName: Corneal ectasia predominantly in the inferior cornea
searchTerms: cornea bulging mainly in lower part

common.symptomName: Corneal protrusion adjacent to the area of thinning
searchTerms: cornea sticking out near thin area
localized corneal bulge adjacent to thinning

occasional.symptomName: Corneal hydrops due to acute rupture of Descemet's membrane
searchTerms: sudden corneal swelling from membrane rupture
corneal edema due to Descemet's break

occasional.symptomName: Mild ocular discomfort or foreign body sensation

searchTerms: seeing halos or glare around lights
vision with light rings or glare

rare.symptomName: Corneal scarring secondary to chronic ectasia
searchTerms: scarring on cornea due to ectasia
new blood vessels growing in cornea
abnormal blood vessel growth in eye

imaging: Corneal topography showing inferior steepening with 'kissing dove' or 'crab claw' pattern
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating peripheral corneal thinning
Slit-lamp examination revealing inferior corneal thinning band
genetic: No definitive genetic markers identified; familial cases reported but inheritance pattern unclear
other: Absence of corneal scarring differentiates from other ectatic disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Central or paracentral corneal thinning rather than inferior peripheral thinning
Different corneal topography pattern (asymmetric bowtie with inferior steepening)
More frequent corneal scarring and hydrops
Peripheral corneal thinning with lipid deposition

redFlags: Rapid progression of corneal thinning and ectasia
Sudden significant decrease in visual acuity
references: Krachmer JH, Feder RS, Belin MW. Keratoconus and related noninflammatory corneal thinning disorders. Surv Ophthalmol. 1984;28(4):293-322.
